subject: english
title: 2027年河南新高考模拟试卷　英语
reference_notes: Q1–5参照2025、2026全国一卷短对话单段单题的口语篇幅，设置事实、场景、要义、时间及观点题。借用绘图设备、寄件、投影反馈、接人时间和手机支架是独立原创情境。
Q6–10参照2025全国一卷长对话中的最初情形与后来行动、时间或数量推算，以及2026全国一卷第6–10题的理由、预约细节和后续手续。新设语言交流小组与羽毛球场地预约。
Q11–16参照2025、2026全国一卷相应长话中的看法、转折、访谈动机及结果，区分朋友建议与实际决定、写作者期待与现场反应。图书领取柜与可拼合托盘为原创设定。
Q17–20采用2026全国一卷的末段独白四题规模，取主题、条件动作、用意和提交物四个观察点。历史课模拟访谈为原创情境。所有原稿为单遍稿。

listening.L01:
M: Could I borrow your tablet for my sketching class? My phone screen is too small.
W: My tablet's at work. Take my old laptop. It's got the drawing program you need.
M: Great. I'll bring it back after class.
listening.L02:
W: I'd like this to get to my sister by Friday. Does it cost extra for her to sign for it?
M: Yes. Let me weigh the box first. Then I can tell you which service will get it there in time.
listening.L03:
W: Could you see my slides from the last row?
M: The titles were fine. The photos were too small to see, though. I could hear you just fine.
W: Good. I'll put one big picture on each slide next time.
listening.L04:
M: I should pick Lila up at 4:30, right?
W: That's when her piano lesson starts today. The teacher's adding fifteen minutes to the usual half hour. Could you be there when she's done?
M: Sure.
listening.L05:
W: I ordered this phone stand because it folds up easily. But every time I touch the screen, the whole thing falls over.
M: Can you send it back?
W: I hope so. I've only had it since Monday.
listening.L06:
M: How was the language exchange, Tessa? Did you try the advanced group?
W: I did. People spoke so quickly that I could barely get a sentence in. Jon took me over to his table. They pulled questions from a bag and took turns answering them. I ended up talking for five minutes about my grandmother's dog.
M: Will you go back to the advanced group next time?
W: I'll stay with Jon's group for a while. He's asked me to write a few questions for the bag.
listening.L07:
W: Maple Sports Center. How can I help you?
M: Hi. I'm calling for the badminton group. We expected sixteen players on Sunday, but four have pulled out. Can we still get courts at 10:00?
W: You can. Four players to a court. I can put all your courts next to one another upstairs, or there are two downstairs and one upstairs.
M: Let's stay together. Do you lend out rackets? One of us is new and doesn't have one.
W: I can put one aside for him. He'll need to leave an ID at reception while he uses it.
M: Great. I'll mention that in the group message. Can I pay when we turn up?
W: Yes. I'll text you the booking number now. Just show it when you come in.
listening.L08:
M: Did you read the library's note about the lockers by the side door?
W: I did. When a book you've requested is ready, they'll send you a number. You enter it at a locker and get your book, even if the front desk has closed.
M: Sounds as if the library could close the desk earlier, then.
W: That would be a shame. Last week I went in to look for a book on local buildings. I only knew part of the title, and the woman at the desk found it for me. I'd use the lockers for books I've already requested. I'd still want someone to talk to when I'm looking for something.
M: The library's collecting comments until tomorrow. Want to send that in?
W: Good idea. I'll write it this evening.
listening.L09:
M: Welcome to Small Inventions. I'm speaking to Mia Reed, who designs jigsaw puzzles. Mia, where did you get the idea for the puzzles you make for train stations?
W: It came from my grandfather. He liked doing the puzzle in the hospital waiting room. Whenever he left to see my grandmother, he had to put the puzzle away so other people could use the table. He hardly ever got to finish it.
M: How did you make yours different?
W: I kept the same number of pieces. I divided the picture into six scenes and put each scene in its own tray. You can finish one scene and leave. When you fit the trays together, you get six views of a single street.
M: What surprised you when you tried it at Hillford Station?
W: We thought travelers would work quietly on their own, but they kept asking strangers about the scenes in the other trays. Some even stayed to see the trays put together.
listening.L10:
W: Hi, everyone. I'm Ms. Turner from the history department. Next week you'll record short interviews with former employees of the old Weston bus factory. This afternoon is practice. Your partner will play the guest. Next to the recorder there's a list of questions. Keep it nearby and let the other person finish speaking before you look down at it. If they mention something that surprises you, ask them to tell you more. You can return to the printed questions later.

Some of you asked about taking video. For today, just record the sound. Put one of the old factory photos on the table between you before you start. Your partner may find it easier to remember details when there's something from that time to look at. After your practice interview, listen to the first minute together. Then write down one thing you want to do differently and hand me the note on your way out. Save the recording for tomorrow.
